rationale: Bounded injectivity proof for String values ≤256 bytes is proportionate to P1 scope. Kani harness with tracking mock correctly models the property (input discrimination, not hash completeness). GOD RULE #1 compliance noted: harness must use kani::any() not hardcoded inputs. Unwind bound of 3 is appropriate for shallow match nesting.

Integer injectivity proof (i64::to_le_bytes bijection) is well-scoped. Kani can exhaustively explore the i64 domain. Unwind 2 is appropriate (single match arm, no nested loops). This is a regression-proof that the encoding remains injective through refactoring.

Variant discrimination proof (String vs Integer encoding) is critical for preventing accidental hash collisions. Kani exhaustively explores bounded String≤256 + all i64 pairs. The mock correctly captures the property: different byte sequences → different hash inputs.

Determinism proptest with 10,000 trials provides strong statistical evidence. The pure-function nature of canonical_digest makes this a straightforward property to test. 10,000 trials with 1-10 step workflows covers a meaningful input space.

Defense-in-depth proptest for Finish result sensitivity complements Kani bounded proofs by exploring larger input spaces (proptest is unbounded in practice). Two independent layers (Kani formal + proptest statistical) provide robust coverage of the same contract clause.
Position sensitivity proptest exercises step reordering which is a structural property of the step iteration loop. Validates that canonical_digest() is order-sensitive as specified in contract C3.

End-to-end integration test closes GAP-2 and GAP-6. Covers the full pipeline (parse → compile → digest) verifying that Finish value changes propagate to CompiledWorkflow.digest(). Concrete YAML fixtures provide deterministic, reproducible test cases.
Step ID sensitivity integration test closes GAP-3. Simple, concrete test (rename step id "last" → "done") with clear expected outcome.

Result type discrimination integration test closes GAP-4. Tests the critical distinction between String("42") and Integer(42) through the full compilation pipeline. Complements Kani formal proof of the same property at the encoding level.

Canonical/legacy equivalence test mitigates HAZ-1 (duplicate code divergence). Critical for ensuring proptest helpers using the legacy path produce digests matching production code. May require visibility changes (pub(super) or #[cfg(test)] re-export for the legacy path).

Exhaustiveness test for ScalarValue handling closes GAP-5 and mitigates HAZ-2. While the obligation is a runtime test (not compile-time enforcement via removing the _ arm), it provides adequate defense for the current 2-variant enum. Finding PPF-FINISH-003 notes the bounds description should clarify runtime vs compile-time semantics.
Unsafe/IO/random audit is a well-scoped static analysis using grep. The command is exact and auditable. Complements the #![forbid(unsafe_code)] crate-level attribute.

Pre-validation digest scope proptest validates that IR layout changes do not affect digest (C9). The structural guarantee (function takes &WorkflowSource, not &CompiledWorkflow) provides strong inherent proof, but the proptest adds defense-in-depth. Finding PPF-FINISH-001 notes the bounds field is vague — acceptable for P1 given the structural guarantee.

NOT_APPLICABLE decision is well-supported. Digest computation is a pure stateless function. The digest lifecycle is a purely sequential pipeline (parsed→digest→lowered→validated→persisted) with zero interleavings, zero concurrent paths, zero retry loops. boundary-map.md confirms no concurrency, no async, no IO. workflow-model.md confirms sequential states with no temporal hazards requiring state-machine model checking. TLA+'s core strength (concurrent state-machine interleaving analysis) has no application here.

NOT_APPLICABLE decision is proportionate for P1. Verus is designed for Rust-local invariants with Verus-compatible data structures. The digest's core dependency (blake3::Hasher) is external and not Verus-verified. The properties (injectivity, determinism, variant discrimination) are behavioral, not type-refinement. Proving them in Verus would require ghost modeling of blake3 internals — disproportionate for a ~22-line function. Kani (bounded input proofs) + proptest (statistical) + integration tests provide adequate P1 coverage. The NOT_APPLICABLE evidence correctly identifies this as a behavioral rather than refinement concern.

NOT_APPLICABLE decision is correct. Flux refines data-level numeric/index predicates (bounds checks, non-zero values, range constraints). The properties here are function-level (injectivity, determinism) that Flux cannot express. The existing types (ScalarValue enum, WorkflowDigest [u8;32] repr(transparent)) are already type-safe; no data refinements on top of the Rust type system are needed.

NOT_APPLICABLE decision is fully evidenced. Digest subsystem has zero concurrency: no threads, no async, no channels, no atomics, no locks. canonical_digest is a pure synchronous function. boundary-map.md confirms this at the Async Boundary section. Loom's permutation-based concurrency testing has no target.

NOT_APPLICABLE decision is correct. Both vb_compile and vb_core have #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (verified via grep). No raw pointers, no FFI, no MaybeUninit, no interior mutability in the digest path. Miri's UB detection has no unsafe code to analyze.

NOT_APPLICABLE decision is sound. The digest function operates on typed AST (WorkflowSource, StepPrimitive, ScalarValue), not raw bytes. Fuzzing raw bytes would require routing through the YAML parser (out of scope). Proptest (generates typed values) and Kani (exhaustive bounded exploration) provide better coverage for typed APIs than byte-level fuzzing.
